why: A `.m` that is one whole-file `%{ … %}` block comment is a MATLAB script of comments, the same as an empty one (the user's ruling (step 11)): a statement naming it runs it, so `notes` in `main` links to it, and a call with an argument is an error in MATLAB ('Attempt to execute SCRIPT … as a function'), so `notes(1)` in `user` links nowhere and is a live row (matlab-resolution.test.ts 'takes the nearest file of the name, script or function; a call with arguments that finds a script first reaches nothing'). A file whose first comment is `%` help text is a help-text stub (the stub rule, matlab-lookup step 8; matlab-resolution.test.ts 'MATLAB stubs: the help text of a MEX function'), and a file of block comments only is a script: once the step puts a `%` line before the block, the file is help text, so the call with an argument links to it too, and the statement still does.
